newsitem.title: USA: Illinois man charged with Rams' Harris pleads guilty.
newsitem.headline: Illinois man charged with Rams' Harris pleads guilty.

text.p: One of four men arrested along with St. Louis Rams defensive end James Harris on cocaine charges pleaded guilty Tuesday in federal court.
Dwight Flowers Jr., 30, of Chesterfield, Mo., had been charged with intent to buy and distribute cocaine and crack cocaine. The indictment disclosed Monday said Harris was the financier of the deal.
Harris was freed on $750,000 bond Monday and was back at the Rams' training camp in Macomb, Ill.
His agent Harold Lewis said Harris was at the "wrong place, at the wrong time" when he and the others were arrested over the weekend at an East St. Louis home.
Lewis said Harris was picking up a friend to go car-shopping at the time of the police raid and that was why he was carrying $52,000 in cash.

Harris starred in high school sports in East St. Louis and maintained a home there. Federal prosecutors said they planned to argue that Harris be jailed prior to trial at his next hearing, scheduled for Aug. 8.
In February, Harris signed a three-year contract with the Rams paying him roughly $1 million per season.
